analyst_view.overall: Iberia 1999 (29th of 36, 1 point) host Getafe (30th, 1 point) in Tbilisi; Iberia, top of the Georgian league, lean on striker Amiran Dzagania, while Getafe need a win to keep any top-24 hope. Getafe lost 3-0 to Atlético on Sunday, sit just above the LaLiga drop zone and go to Espanyol on Monday; Bordalás said after the Brighton defeat that league football is the priority, so a changed side is likely. Getafe trained on Tuesday with most of the first team, including Mayoral, Ünal and Satriano; Djené, banned for Monday's league game after his red against Atlético, is free to play here. Carvajal, Boselli, Juanmi and Uche are out and in the numbers, and Andrés García is a doubt after asking off against Atlético. Romanian referee Horațiu Feșnic is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Getafe. Bordalás has openly put the league first, with a must-win trip to Espanyol on Monday, so Getafe are likely to rotate and keep their usual low-risk game, which the numbers can't see; I go to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, 5.1 for Getafe. A rotated Getafe side still plays direct with crosses into the box, so the count should hold; I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high because Getafe foul a lot and referee Horațiu Feșnic has shown 5.5 a game in his two on record. Getafe's style does not change with rotation, and Djené, freshly sent off in LaLiga, is likely to play, but that is already Getafe's normal profile, so I stay at 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, nearly 16 for Getafe. An expected reserve-heavy Getafe side with league priorities should be more cautious, so I trim to about 23.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. With Getafe likely to rest some starters before Espanyol and Juanmi and Uche out (already counted), I go a little lower, to about 7.7.
